newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil closes lower on deliveries, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil closes lower on deliveries, exports.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed lower on deliveries on the December contract plus scant exports, traders said.

The soyoil delivery tally was at 2,750 lots of soyoil against the December contract. But the market was expecting between 2,000 and 4,000 lots to be posted which muted the bearishness of the delivery market.
USDA's weekly export sales report showed U.S. net sales of soyoil during the week ended Nov 21 at 14,700 tonnes. The market was expecting from 20,000 to 50,000 tonnes.
Soymeal closed mixed with nearby December closing higher.
There were no deliveries posted Friday against the December contract amid tight nearby stocks of soymeal.

Gains in soymeal were limited by a lighter-than-expected number for soymeal in USDA's weekly export sales report. USDA said U.S. net export sales of soymeal during the week ended November 21 were at 77,000 tonnes.
The market was expecting from 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
Soyoil closed 0.20 to 0.41 cent lower, with December down 0.25 at 22.98 cents a lb. Soymeal settled $0.90 higher to $0.70 lower, with December up $0.90 at $239.50 per tonne.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, below the 35,978 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, below the 19,643 traded Wednesday.
